# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

For two weeks matters proceeded without a hitch in the Good-Conduct Club. It appeared to function wonderfully. Kit Carrow was not summoned as arbiter even one time. Not a single time did any of the manse youngsters stir up the Glen gossips. Regarding their smaller home offenses, they monitored one another strictly and bravely endured their self-assigned penalties—usually choosing not to attend some lively Friday evening gathering in Fern Hollow, or remaining in bed during some spring night when every youthful body longed to be outside roaming. Grace, because she whispered in Sunday School, sentenced herself to spend an entire day without uttering a solitary word, except if it was completely required, and carried it out. It was somewhat unlucky that Mr. Pratt from over-harbour selected that particular night to visit the manse, and that Grace chanced to answer the door. She did not answer a single word to his friendly welcome, but departed without a sound to fetch her father concisely. Mr. Pratt felt a bit insulted and informed his wife upon returning home that the eldest Ashdown girl appeared to be a remarkably timid, moody young person, lacking sufficient manners to reply when addressed. However, no greater trouble resulted from it, and usually their punishments caused no damage to themselves or anyone else. Every one of them was starting to feel utterly confident that, as it turned out, raising yourself was a remarkably simple task.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0000 }

“I suppose everyone will shortly realize that we are capable of conducting ourselves just as appropriately as anyone else,” Grace declared exultantly. “It is not difficult once we set our focus on it.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0001 }

Ida and she were perched upon the Pollock tombstone. Fern Hollow was far too unsuitable for girls due to the cold, raw, wet conditions of a spring storm, even though the boys from the manse and Hollowmere had gone down there to fish. Although the rain had paused, a brutal east wind swept in from the sea, piercing straight to the bone and marrow. Despite its initial promise, spring was tardy, and a firm drift of old ice and snow remained even now in the northern corner of the graveyard. Shivering, Zilla Marsh, who had walked up to deliver a mess of herring to the manse, slipped through the gate. She came from the fishing village situated at the harbour mouth, and for thirty years, her father had maintained the habit of sending a mess to the manse from his initial spring catch. Never entering a church door, he was a heavy drinker and a wild man; nevertheless, provided he dispatched those herring to the manse each spring, just as his father had done prior to him, he felt pleasantly certain that his standing with the Powers That Govern was settled for the year. Had he failed to send the season's first fruits in this manner, he would not have anticipated a profitable mackerel catch.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0002 }

Though Zilla had reached a decade of age, her tiny, shriveled frame made her appear even younger. She crept toward the manse girls with a certain bravery this evening, looking as though warmth had eluded her during her entire existence. A purple hue covered her visage, while her pale-blue, audacious little eyes appeared red and filled with tears. Dressed in a torn print garment, she had a frayed woolen comforter fastened over her skinny shoulders and beneath her arms. The journey of three miles from the harbour mouth had been made on her bare feet, along a path still covered in snow, slush, and mud. A purple tone, matching her face, marked her feet and legs. Yet Zilla was not greatly bothered by these conditions. Coldness was familiar to her, and her bare feet had already endured a month of exposure, just like the rest of the teeming young offspring in the fishing village. Pitying herself was far from her thoughts when she placed herself upon the tombstone and offered a bright smile to Grace and Ida. Grace and Ida responded with cheerful smiles of their own. Their acquaintance with Zilla was slight, rooted in a couple of encounters during the previous summer when a trip down the harbour had been taken with the Carrows.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0003 }

“Hello!” said Zilla, “isn’t the night quite wild? It is not suitable for a dog to be outside, is it?”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0004 }

“Then what brings you outside?” Grace inquired.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0005 }

“Pa made me bring you up some herring,” Zilla answered back. She trembled, gave a cough, and extended her bare feet. Zilla was not dwelling on herself or her feet, nor was she attempting to gain any sympathy. She extended her feet purely by instinct so they would not touch the damp grass surrounding the tombstone. However, Grace and Ida were immediately overwhelmed by a surge of compassion for her. She appeared so cold—so unhappy.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0006 }

“Oh, on a night so cold, why are you barefoot?” Grace exclaimed. “Almost frozen, your feet must be.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0007 }

“Almost,” Zilla declared with pride. “I’m telling you, trekking up that harbour road was brutal.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0008 }

“Why didn’t you put your shoes and stockings on?” Ida asked.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0009 }

“There isn’t any to wear. Everything I owned was completely worn out when winter ended,” Zilla remarked with indifference.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0010 }

Grace stared in horror for a moment. It was terrible. A little girl, who was almost a neighbour, was half frozen in this cruel spring weather because she lacked shoes or stockings. Impulsive Grace could think of nothing except how dreadful it was. She was pulling off her own shoes and stockings in a moment.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0011 }

“Here, put these on immediately,” she urged, shoving the garments upon the bewildered Zilla. “Hurry up. A fatal chill will come over you. More are in my possession. Put these on right now.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0012 }

Regaining her senses, Zilla grabbed the presented present, a gleam appearing in her lifeless eyes. Certainly she intended to wear them, and exceedingly fast, prior to the arrival of anybody with the power to take them back. Within sixty seconds, she had drawn the stockings across her thin small legs and slid the shoes of Grace over her stout small ankles.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0013 }

“I am grateful to you,” she remarked, “however will your people not be angry?”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0014 }

“No—and their identity doesn't matter to me,” Grace stated. “Is it possible you believe I could watch a person freeze to death and not assist them if it were in my power? Doing so would be wrong, particularly since a minister is what my father is.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0015 }

“Will you need them returned? Down at the harbour mouth, it is terribly cold—well after this place has warmed up,” Zilla noted cunningly.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0016 }

“No, you are supposed to retain them, naturally. My intention when presenting them was precisely that. Another pair of shoes and a large quantity of stockings belong to me.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0017 }

Zilla had intended to remain for a time to discuss numerous topics with the girls. Nevertheless, she currently felt it was wiser to depart prior to anyone arriving to force her to surrender her spoils. Consequently, she moved away through the freezing dusk using the same quiet, elusive manner in which she had arrived. Once the manse was no longer within view, she seated herself, removed the shoes and stockings, and placed them inside her herring basket. Wearing them along that filthy harbour road was not something she planned to do. Their purpose was to be preserved in good condition for special events. No other young girl near the harbour mouth possessed such splendid black cashmere stockings and such stylish, barely worn shoes. Zilla was fully equipped for the summer season. She experienced no feelings of guilt regarding the situation. To her mind, the individuals at the manse possessed immense wealth, and those girls unquestionably owned an abundance of shoes and stockings. Afterward, Zilla hurried down to the Glen village where she engaged in play for an hour with the boys in front of Mr. Flagg’s store, wading through a puddle of slush alongside the wilder children, right up to the moment Mrs. Kerr arrived and ordered her to go home.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0018 }

“Grace, I do not believe you ought to have performed that action,” Ida remarked with mild reproof once Zilla had departed. “Now it will be necessary for you to put on your fine boots daily, and before long they will become scuffed.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0019 }

“I don’t care,” exclaimed Grace, who was yet experiencing the wonderful warmth that comes from performing a good deed for someone else. “It is not right for me to possess two pairs of shoes while poor little Zilla Marsh does not own even one. We each possess a pair now. You are well aware, Ida, of what father stated during his sermon this past Sunday concerning how genuine joy is never found in acquiring or possessing things—it comes solely through giving. That is absolute truth. At this moment, I am conscious of a much greater happiness than I have ever experienced at any previous time in my life. Imagine Zilla traveling toward home at this exact second, her unfortunate small feet now feeling completely comfortable, cozy, and warm.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0020 }

“You are aware that you do not own a second pair of black cashmere stockings,” Ida stated. “Aunt Martha declared that your alternate pair had too many holes for her to mend again, so she sliced the legs into stove dusters. All you possess are those couple of pairs of striped stockings that you despise.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0021 }

Grace lost every bit of her radiance and inspiration. The joy she felt deflated just like a punctured balloon. For several gloomy minutes, she remained seated without speaking, confronting the repercussions of her hasty deed.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0022 }

“Oh, Ida, that had not occurred to me,” she remarked mournfully. “I failed to pause and reflect whatsoever.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0023 }

Aunt Martha had knitted blue and red striped stockings for Grace during the winter, which were thick, heavy, coarse, and ribbed. Unquestionably, they were hideous. Grace's hatred for them surpassed any dislike she had ever felt previously. She was determined not to wear them under any circumstances. In her bureau drawer, they remained completely unused.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0024 }

“After this, wearing the striped stockings will be necessary for you,” Ida said. “Only imagine how much you will be laughed at by the boys at school. The way they make fun of Mamie Warren because of her striped stockings and nickname her barber pole is familiar to you, and the ones you have are much worse.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0025 }

“I refuse to put them on,” Grace declared. “Despite the chill, I’d rather go without shoes.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0026 }

“Tomorrow, you are unable to attend church without shoes. Consider what folks would think.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0027 }

“I will remain at home then.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0028 }

“It is impossible for you to refrain. You are fully aware that Aunt Martha is going to force your attendance.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0029 }

Grace was aware of this. Aunt Martha made a point of demanding only one thing: everyone had to attend church, regardless of the weather. She was indifferent to how they were attired, or whether they had clothes on at all. Nevertheless, their attendance was mandatory. Seven decades in the past, Aunt Martha was raised in this exact manner, and she intended to raise them in the very same way.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0030 }

“Can you not lend me a pair, Ida?” asked poor Grace in a piteous manner.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0031 }

Shaking her head, Ida responded, “No, you are aware that I possess just a single black pair. Moreover, because they are exceedingly tight, I struggle to put them on. They would fail to fit you. My gray ones would not fit either. Furthermore, their legs are covered in repeated darning.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0032 }

“I will not put on those striped stockings,” Grace declared obstinately. “How they feel is still worse than how they look. They give me the sensation that my legs have grown as large as barrels, plus they are extremely scratchy.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0033 }

“Well, I am unaware of what your plans are.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0034 }

“Were father at home, I would head over and request that he purchase a fresh pair for me prior to the shop’s shutting. However, he will not return until it is far too late. My request will have to wait until Monday—and I am not attending church tomorrow. Feigning illness will be my strategy, leaving Aunt Martha with no choice but to permit me to remain at home.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0035 }

“To do that would be living a falsehood, Grace,” Ida exclaimed. “It is impossible for you to do so. You are aware of how terrible it would be. How would father react if he found out? Have you forgotten his words to us following mother's death, when he instructed us to remain truthful above all other shortcomings? He stated that we must never speak or live a falsehood—he mentioned he was counting on us to refrain from it. You cannot proceed with this, Grace. Simply put on the striped stockings. The situation will last for just one occasion. No one is going to observe them during the service. The setting is different from school. Furthermore, they will hardly be visible beneath your long new brown dress. Wasn't it fortunate that Aunt Martha crafted it large to allow space for your growth, despite how much you disliked it upon its completion?”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0036 }

“Those stockings are something I will not wear,” Grace said once more. After unwinding her pale, unclothed legs from the gravestone, she intentionally strode across the damp, icy turf toward the snowbank. Clenching her jaw, she placed her feet on the snow and remained standing.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0037 }

“What are you doing?” Ida exclaimed, horrified. “Grace Ashdown, you’ll catch your death of cold.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0038 }

“I am attempting to do so,” Grace replied. “My wish is that I contract a terrible cold and become terribly ill on the following day. If that happens, my behavior will not be deceitful. My plan is to remain standing in this spot for as long as I am able to endure it.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0039 }

“However, Grace, your life could actually be in danger. Pneumonia could catch you. Grace, I beg you, do not do this. We ought to step inside and find a remedy for your feet. Ah, Tobias has arrived. My gratitude is immense. Tobias, compel Grace to step away from the snow. Observe her feet.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0040 }

“Holy cats! Grace, what are you doing?” Tobias demanded. “Are you crazy?”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0041 }

“No. Go away!” Grace snapped.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0042 }

“Are you, in that case, inflicting punishment on yourself for a reason? Should you be doing so, it is not correct. You will become ill.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0043 }

“I desire to throw up. Punishing myself is not what I am doing. Leave.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0044 }

“Where are her stockings and shoes?” Tobias inquired of Ida.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0045 }

“They were given to Zilla Marsh by her.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0046 }

“Zilla Marsh? Why?”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0047 }

“Since Zilla possessed none—and her feet felt very freezing. Also, she desires to become ill at present to avoid attending church the next day and putting on her striped stockings. Nevertheless, Tobias, she might perish.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0048 }

“Grace,” Tobias said, “step away from that ice-bank, otherwise I will drag you off it.”
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0049 }

“Pull away,” Grace dared.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0050 }

Tobias leaped toward her and seized her arms. As he tugged in one direction, Grace tugged in the opposite direction. Ida hurried up from behind Grace and shoved. Grace yelled furiously at Tobias to leave her alone. Tobias yelled right back at her not to be a dizzy idiot; and Ida began to weep. A great deal of clamor was made by them, and they were near the graveyard's road fence. Driving past, Henry Warren and his wife both heard them and saw them. It was not long before the Glen was told that a terrible brawl had occurred among the manse children in the graveyard, complete with the use of most improper language. In the meantime, Grace had permitted herself to be dragged off the ice, for her feet were hurting so intensely that she was willing to leave it by any means. All of them went inside amicably and retired to bed. Grace had the sleep of a cherub and awakened the next morning without the slightest sign of a cold. Recalling that long-ago conversation with her father, she felt unable to pretend to be ill and live a falsehood. Nevertheless, her resolve remained just as strong as it had ever been that those abominable stockings would not be worn by her to church.
{: #nw-v05-c24-p0051 }
